paper_metadata.title: Resting-State Functional Connectivity Alterations Associated with Six-Month Outcomes in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a well-defined prospective multicenter cohort (TRACK-TBI) with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and a matched control group. The sample is representative of the mTBI population seen in emergency departments.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: A sample of 75 mTBI patients recruited at San Francisco General Hospital (SFGH) as part of the prospective multi-center Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in TBI (TRACK-TBI) pilot study was included in this investigation.
items.reasoning: The source is a specific trauma center within a larger prospective study, providing a clear context for the target population.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The inclusion criteria included CT scan to assess for evidence of acute TBI within 24 h of injury, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score 13–15 (upon emergency department [ED] arrival), loss of consciousness (LOC) <30 min, post-traumatic amnesia (PTA) duration <24 h, and age 18–55 years (inclusive).
items.reasoning: Recruitment was based on objective clinical criteria in an ED setting, which is standard for mTBI prognosis studies.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (rsfMRI connectivity) is measured using standardized, state-of-the-art neuroimaging protocols and objective automated analysis (ICA/FIX), minimizing measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: A 7 min. rsfMRI single shot gradient-echo echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence was acquired (repetition time [TR] = 2000 ms, echo time [TE] = 28 ms; flip angle = 90 grad; field of view [FOV] = 220 mm; voxel size = 3.4 x 3.4 x 4.0 mm).
items.reasoning: The imaging parameters and the definition of functional connectivity are precisely described.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: We then used ICA-based Xnoiseifier artifact removal (FIX) to de-noise single subject data... a group-level ICA was performed in the new ''clean'' data
items.reasoning: The use of validated FSL tools and FIX artifact removal ensures high reliability of the connectivity measures.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: each edge represents the connectivity between pairs of nodes, computed using full correlation.
items.reasoning: Connectivity is treated as a continuous variable (Z-scores/correlations) rather than arbitrary categories.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: all MRIs were performed on the same 3T GE Signa EXCITE scanner... using the same scanner software version.
items.reasoning: The study used a single scanner and identical protocol for all subjects, eliminating site/hardware bias.
